key_insight: Independent DFT databases disagree enough to set a measurable error floor for universal MLIPs, and the best model matches that baseline.
engineering_relevance: Alloy-screening workflows should check elemental references and benchmark against cross-database disagreement before trusting model rankings.
method: Benchmark 14 universal MLIPs on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, unseen during training.
Compare energy and stability errors with disagreement among AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD.
Re-reference energies and screen broken elemental references to test ranking robustness.
evidence_signal: For half the structures, DFT databases differ by less than 6–8 meV/atom, but larger outliers raise average disagreement to 16–30 meV/atom; after re-referencing, the best MLIP agrees with AFLOW as closely as Alexandria does.
watch_item: Agreement with AFLOW is not proof of absolute accuracy because DFT reference uncertainty limits how confidently small model differences can be ranked.
paper_title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
